topics.name: Supervisor Pattern
topics.description: A coordinator agent routing work to specialists.
notes: - 一个 supervisor agent 负责理解任务、拆分并路由给专门的 worker agent。
- worker 只关注自己的领域（如检索、写代码），拥有各自的工具和提示词。
- supervisor 收集结果后决定继续派发还是给出最终答案。
- 优点：职责清晰，易于扩展新的 worker，便于调试。
- 缺点：supervisor 是中心节点，多一次模型调用，延迟和成本更高。
- 单个 agent 工具过多、提示词过长导致效果下降时，才需要拆成多 agent。

topics.name: Handoffs
notes: - Handoff 是一个 agent 把控制权（以及必要的上下文）交给另一个 agent。
- 在 LangGraph 中常用 Command(goto=..., update=...) 实现。
- 需要决定把完整历史还是摘要传给下一个 agent，避免上下文污染和 token 浪费。
- 交接后要明确由谁向用户回复，并设置终止条件，避免 agent 之间来回互相转交。

questions.title: What is the role of the supervisor in a supervisor multi-agent system?

options.text: It routes tasks to specialized agents and decides when the work is finished
It stores all documents in a vector database
It replaces the need for tools
It trains the worker agents

questions.explanation: The supervisor coordinates. Workers do the specialized work with their own tools and prompts.

questions.title: Which are good reasons to split a single agent into several agents?

options.text: One agent has so many tools that it often picks the wrong one
Different tasks need different prompts or models
Multi-agent systems are always faster and cheaper
You want to develop and test components independently

questions.explanation: Splitting helps focus and modularity, but adds model calls, latency and cost, so start with a single agent when it is enough.

questions.title: What is a typical downside of the supervisor pattern?

options.text: Extra model calls for routing add latency and cost
Workers cannot use tools
State cannot be shared
It only works with one worker

questions.explanation: Every routing decision is another model call, and the supervisor is a central point that can become a bottleneck.

questions.title: What does this node do?

options.text: It updates the topic key and routes execution to the billing node
It only updates the state; routing is decided elsewhere
It ends the graph
It calls the billing node as a normal Python function and waits

questions.explanation: Command combines a state update with a goto, which is the usual way to implement a handoff.

questions.title: The run never finishes and eventually fails with a recursion error. Why?

options.text: The agents hand off to each other forever; add a condition that routes to END
Command cannot use goto
The state schema is missing
Handoffs require a checkpointer

questions.explanation: Without a termination condition the agents ping-pong until the recursion limit is hit. Decide who produces the final answer and route to END.

questions.title: What should you consider passing to the next agent in a handoff?

options.text: Only the context it needs, such as a summary, to avoid bloating the prompt
Always the entire raw history of every agent
Nothing; agents must never share information
The API keys of the previous agent

questions.explanation: Passing too much wastes tokens and can confuse the next agent. Passing too little loses necessary context.
